description: A Snowflake Scripting variable referenced inside a scalar construct the procedural builder does NOT model with a dedicated node - a :: or CAST cast, CASE, IN, BETWEEN - must resolve to the variable's VALUE. Previously such constructs were evaluated as a standalone SELECT <text> that could not see procedural variables, so w::VARCHAR silently returned NULL; they now flow through the shared AST evaluator with the current variables supplied as a resolution context. Pinned across both cast spellings, a cast inside arithmetic, CASE, IN, BETWEEN, the doc pattern that concatenates two casts, and a literal cast as the regression guard. The semi-structured cases are the subtle ones: Snowflake BINDS the variable's value into the statement and THEN compiles the surrounding expression, so a written ::VARIANT still applies - live-verified, ARRAY_CONTAINS(v::VARIANT, arr) answers 'available' and TYPEOF(v::VARIANT) answers VARCHAR, while dropping the cast errors 'Invalid argument types for function ARRAY_CONTAINS: (VARCHAR(1), VARIANT)', which reports the BOUND value's width. Rebuilding the call from argument VALUES alone dropped the cast, so the strict semi-structured families rejected the bare VARCHAR literal that substitution had created - and the last test keeps that rule firing. Converted 1:1 from scripting/ScriptVariableInScalarConstructTest (now retired).

steps.sql: BEGIN LET w INTEGER := 168; RETURN w::VARCHAR; END;
BEGIN LET w INTEGER := 168; RETURN CAST(w AS VARCHAR); END;
BEGIN LET w VARCHAR := '168'; RETURN w::NUMBER + 1; END;
BEGIN LET w INTEGER := 168; RETURN CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN w ELSE 99 END; END;
BEGIN LET w INTEGER := 168; RETURN w IN (1, 168, 200); END;
BEGIN LET w INTEGER := 168; RETURN w BETWEEN 1 AND 200; END;
BEGIN LET w INTEGER := 168; LET dt DATE := '2020-09-30'; RETURN w::VARCHAR || ', ' || dt::VARCHAR; END;

DECLARE v_target_role VARCHAR := 'ROLE_CALLER'; role_array VARIANT; BEGIN SELECT PARSE_JSON('["ROLE_CALLER","OTHER"]') INTO role_array; IF (NOT ARRAY_CONTAINS(v_target_role::VARIANT, role_array)) THEN RETURN 'NOT available'; END IF; RETURN 'available'; END;
BEGIN LET v VARCHAR := 'abc'; RETURN TYPEOF(v::VARIANT); END;
BEGIN LET v VARCHAR := 'abc'; RETURN ARRAY_CONTAINS(v, PARSE_JSON('["abc"]')); END;
